premium-medspa-seo-audit.title: Technical SEO Audit & Local Optimization for U.S.-Based Medical Spa
premium-medspa-seo-audit.summary: Resolved critical technical SEO issues blocking Google indexation and developed comprehensive local SEO strategy.
premium-medspa-seo-audit.tags: Technical SEO • Local SEO • Site Audit
premium-medspa-seo-audit.challenge: A medical spa website was experiencing poor visibility despite offering premium services. Initial investigation revealed that SEO metadata (titles & descriptions) were not appearing in the HTML source due to a plugin conflict between RankMath and Yoast SEO. Additionally, canonical tags were misconfigured, some self-referenced incorrectly, while others pointed to local development domains instead of the live site. These issues prevented Google from properly crawling, indexing, and ranking the site's service pages.
premium-medspa-seo-audit.approach: Conducted a comprehensive SEO audit covering technical, on-page, and local SEO factors. Built an SEO Implementation Tracking Sheet to organize all optimizations and monitor progress. Resolved the metadata visibility issue by deactivating RankMath and maintaining Yoast SEO as the single source of truth. Fixed all canonical tag errors to ensure each page properly referenced its authoritative URL. Drafted optimized titles, meta descriptions, and heading structures for service and location pages. Developed a detailed Local SEO Strategy covering on-page optimization, local citations, link building, and content strategy.

local-seo-guide-businesses.title: The Complete Local SEO Guide for Service Businesses
local-seo-guide-businesses.excerpt: A practical guide to Google Business Profile, local keywords and reviews, so nearby customers find you first.
local-seo-guide-businesses.content:
By Mohamed Toudghi – SEO & Digital Marketing Specialist

If you run a service-based business and want more customers from Google Search and Google Maps, Local SEO is one of the highest-ROI channels you can invest in.

Whether you’re a clinic, a restaurant, a real estate agency, or a service provider, your potential customers are already searching for you online.

This guide will show you, step by step, how to improve local SEO so you can rank higher, generate more leads, and build a trusted reputation. I’ll focus on practical tactics, backed by data, that work for businesses in any local market.

1. Why Local SEO Matters

Local search is no longer just “nice to have”. It’s how people make real buying decisions. If you’re not visible in Google’s Local Pack (the 3–4 map results) or in Maps, you’re losing customers to competitors who are.

2. How Google Local Search Works

Google’s local algorithm is based on three main factors: Proximity, Relevance, and Prominence.

3. Google Business Profile Optimization

Choose one primary category and relevant secondary categories. Avoid irrelevant ones. Regularly upload high-quality images of your team, office, and projects.

4. Local Keyword Research

Target patterns like [Service] + [City]. Language intent matters depending on your target audience.

5. On-Page Local SEO Optimization

  • Location Pages: Create dedicated pages for each city you serve.
  • Title Tags & Meta Descriptions: Include the main service and city name.

6. Local Citations & NAP Consistency

Ensure your Name, Address, and Phone (NAP) are consistent across all platforms.

7. Reviews & Local Trust Signals

Reviews are a core reputation signal. Respond professionally to all feedback.

8. Technical SEO for Local Rankings

Website speed and mobile-friendliness are essential. Implement LocalBusiness Schema Markup.

9. Final Action Plan & Checklist

  • ☐ Claim and verify your Google Business Profile
  • ☐ Standardize your NAP format across the web
  • ☐ Create dedicated city location pages
  • ☐ Implement a review collection process

By following this roadmap, you'll attract more leads and grow your business organically.

why-websites-fail.title: Why Most Websites Fail to Rank on Google (And How to Fix It)
why-websites-fail.excerpt: It's not just about keywords. It's about authority, user experience, and intent.
why-websites-fail.content: Websites often fail to rank not because of a single error, but due to a misalignment between content and search intent. If your page targets a high-volume keyword but doesn't answer the user's specific query, Google will prioritize more relevant competitors. Furthermore, authority is built through consistent, quality backlinks and internal linking structures that demonstrate topical expertise. Ensure your site is technically sound, but never forget that user experience and high-quality, helpful content are the ultimate drivers of search success.

ga4-event-tracking.title: GA4 Event Tracking for Service Websites
ga4-event-tracking.excerpt: How GA4 events work, which ones a service business should track (forms, calls, WhatsApp) and how to set them up with Google Tag Manager.
ga4-event-tracking.content: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) marks a major shift from session-based to event-based tracking. To get the most out of your data, you must move beyond simple pageview metrics. Start by defining your core conversion events, such as form submissions, button clicks, or video views. Use Google Tag Manager to implement these events without modifying code directly. By visualizing your conversion funnel in GA4 Explorations, you can identify precisely where users are dropping off and optimize your site for better performance.

keyword-research-process.title: My 4-Step Keyword Research Process
keyword-research-process.excerpt: How I find low-competition, high-value keywords for any niche.
keyword-research-process.content: Effective keyword research is about finding the intersection of volume, relevance, and difficulty. My 4-step process begins with seed keyword brainstorming based on core business services. Second, I use tools like SEMrush or Ahrefs to analyze competitor rankings and identify 'low-hanging fruit', keywords where competitors are weak. Third, I analyze the SERP intent to ensure we're creating the right type of content (informational vs transactional). Finally, I map these keywords to a content cluster strategy to build topical authority over time.

technical-seo-audit.title: Technical SEO audit for service businesses and SaaS
technical-seo-audit.lead: Google can only rank the pages it can crawl, render and index. I audit your whole site, find what blocks that, and hand you a clear plan ranked by its impact on traffic and leads.

definition.title: What is a technical SEO audit?
paragraphs: A technical SEO audit is a full check of the parts of a website that search engines rely on before they even read the content: crawling, rendering, indexing, site structure, page speed and structured data. It answers one question: can Google reach, understand and trust every page that matters to your business?

A content audit asks whether your pages say the right things. A technical audit asks whether Google can see them at all. When the technical base is broken, new content and new links are wasted, because the pages they point to never get indexed or load too slowly to rank.

For a service business or a SaaS company, the pages that matter are the ones that bring leads: service pages, location pages, pricing, demo and trial pages. My audit starts from those pages and works outwards.

for_who.title: When your site needs a technical SEO audit
items: Your pages do not show up in Google, or show up and then disappear.
Search Console lists pages as “Crawled, currently not indexed” or “Duplicate”.
Your site is slow on mobile or fails Core Web Vitals.
You redesigned or moved the site and traffic dropped.
You want an expert check before you spend more on content or ads.

included.title: What the technical SEO audit includes
included.intro: Every audit covers the same five areas. Each finding comes with the affected URLs, why it matters and how to fix it.

items.name: Full website crawl & technical error analysis
items.desc: I crawl every URL the way Googlebot does and list broken links, redirect chains, server errors, orphan pages and blocked resources.

items.name: Indexing, crawlability & canonical fixes
items.desc: I compare what you want indexed with what Google actually indexes, then fix robots.txt rules, noindex tags, canonical tags and sitemaps so the right version of each page ranks.

items.name: Core Web Vitals & performance recommendations
items.desc: I measure Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift on your real templates and list the changes that move them into the good range.

items.name: Schema & structured data implementation guidance
items.desc: I check your schema.org markup for errors and show which types fit your pages, such as Organization, Service, LocalBusiness, FAQPage or Article.

items.name: Internal linking & site architecture optimization
items.desc: I map how authority flows through your menus and links, find important pages buried too deep, and propose a structure where every service page sits close to the homepage.

steps.title: How the technical SEO audit works

items.title: Access and goals
items.desc: You share access to Google Search Console and, if you have it, Google Analytics. We agree which pages and conversions matter most.

items.title: Crawl and data
items.desc: I crawl the site with Screaming Frog and compare the crawl with your Search Console indexing and performance data.

items.title: Findings ranked by impact
items.desc: Every issue is explained in plain language and ranked by its effect on traffic and leads, so your developer knows what to do first.

items.title: Fixes and checks
items.desc: I fix the issues myself or hand them to your developer with clear instructions, then confirm the results in Search Console.

tools.title: Tools and data behind the audit
tools.intro: An audit is only as good as its data, so I combine a full crawl with Google's own reports.

items.name: Screaming Frog SEO Spider
items.desc: Crawls the site like a search engine and finds technical errors at scale.

items.name: Google Search Console
items.desc: Shows which pages Google indexes, which it rejects and why, and how each page performs in search.

items.name: PageSpeed Insights and Lighthouse
items.desc: Measure Core Web Vitals and loading performance on mobile and desktop.

items.name: Semrush
items.desc: Tracks keyword visibility and site health over time.

items.name: Rich Results Test
items.desc: Checks structured data against Google's requirements.

compare.title: Technical SEO audit vs. full SEO audit
paragraphs: A full SEO audit covers three layers: technical health, content and keywords, and backlinks. A technical SEO audit goes deep on the first layer.

Start with the technical audit when pages are missing from Google, when traffic dropped after a redesign or migration, or when the site is slow. Once the base is solid, content and links finally have something to build on.

faqs.question: What does a technical SEO audit check?
faqs.answer: Everything that affects how Google crawls, indexes and ranks your pages: crawl errors and broken links, indexing and canonical tags, redirects, site structure and internal links, page speed and Core Web Vitals, mobile usability and structured data.

faqs.question: How long does a technical SEO audit take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the size of the site. A small service website is much quicker to audit than a marketplace with thousands of listing pages. You get a clear timeline after the free call.

faqs.question: How much does a technical SEO audit cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the number of pages, the platform and whether you want me to make the fixes. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call, before any work starts.

faqs.question: Do you only report the problems, or also fix them?
faqs.answer: Both are possible. I can fix the issues myself, especially on WordPress, or hand a clear list to your developer and check the work afterwards.

faqs.question: Which platforms do you work with?
faqs.answer: I work a lot with WordPress and Shopify. The audit itself works on any website that Google can crawl.

faqs.question: What do you need from me?
faqs.answer: Access to Google Search Console and, if you have it, Google Analytics. Admin access to the site is only needed if I make the fixes myself.

faqs.question: Can we work in French or Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes. I work in English, French and Arabic, so we can talk in the language you prefer.

local-seo.title: Local SEO for service businesses
local-seo.lead: Show up when people nearby search for what you offer, in the Google map results and the local listings, and turn those searches into calls.

definition.title: What is local SEO?
paragraphs: Local SEO is the work of making a business visible when people search for a service in a specific place, such as “family lawyer Rabat” or “dentist near me”. Google answers these searches with a map, a short list of business profiles and then the regular results.

Google names three factors that decide who appears there: relevance (how well your profile and website match the search), distance (how close you are to the person searching) and prominence (how well known and trusted your business is, through reviews, links and citations). You cannot change your distance, so local SEO works on relevance and prominence.
For a service business, local search is often where the best leads come from: the person searching already knows what they need and is close enough to call today.

for_who.title: Signs your business needs local SEO
items: You do not appear in the map results for your main service in your city.
Competitors with fewer reviews rank above you.
Your business name, address or phone number differ from one directory to another.
You serve several cities but have one generic service page.
Calls and bookings from Google have slowed down.

included.title: What local SEO work includes
included.intro: Five pieces of work, done in the order that brings results fastest.

items.name: Google Business Profile optimization
items.desc: I complete and correct your profile: primary and secondary categories, services, service areas, opening hours, photos and description, so Google knows exactly what you offer and where.

items.name: Citation cleanup & consistency
items.desc: Your business name, address and phone number (NAP) must match on every directory and map. I find and fix the differences that confuse Google and customers.

items.name: Local landing page strategy
items.desc: Each important service and city gets its own useful page with local details, proof and a clear call to action, linked from your profile and menus.

items.name: Review management framework
items.desc: A simple routine for asking happy clients for reviews and replying to every review, because the number, rating and freshness of reviews all feed prominence.

items.name: Local Map Pack visibility improvement
items.desc: I track your positions in the map results for your main searches and adjust the profile, pages and citations until you climb.

items.desc: I check your Google Business Profile, your local rankings and how your name, address and phone appear online.

items.desc: Profile, categories, a useful page for each city and service, and consistent citations.

items.desc: A plan for reviews and local links, with calls and leads from Google tracked.

compare.title: Local SEO vs. traditional SEO
paragraphs: Traditional SEO competes for broad searches with no place in them, often against national websites. Local SEO competes for searches with a place, where your Google Business Profile, reviews and citations matter as much as your website.
Most service businesses need both: local SEO to win nearby customers, and a technically sound website so the service pages linked from the profile can rank and convert.

faqs.question: How long does local SEO take to show results?
faqs.answer: Fixes to your profile and citations can show in the map results within weeks. New pages and reviews build up over months. The pace depends on your city and your competition.

faqs.question: Do I need a website for local SEO?
faqs.answer: A Google Business Profile can rank on its own, but a website with a page for each service and city gives Google more reasons to trust you and gives visitors a place to convert.

faqs.question: How do reviews affect local rankings?
faqs.answer: Reviews are part of prominence. The number of reviews, the rating, how recent they are and whether you reply all help Google and customers trust your business.

faqs.question: Can you help if I serve several cities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each city and service combination usually needs its own useful page, linked from your profile and your main service pages.

faqs.question: How much does local SEO cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on how many locations and services you have. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call, before any work starts.

faqs.answer: Yes. I am based in Morocco, work remotely, and work with businesses in Morocco, the UK and the U.S.

ga4-tracking.title: GA4 and conversion tracking setup
ga4-tracking.lead: See which pages, searches and campaigns bring you leads, not only visits. I set up GA4 and Google Tag Manager properly and build a dashboard you will actually open.

definition.title: What is GA4 conversion tracking?
paragraphs: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) is Google's analytics platform. It records what visitors do on your website as events: a page view, a click on a phone number, a form submission. Conversion tracking means marking the events that create leads, so you can see exactly where those leads come from.
Google Tag Manager sends those events to GA4 and Google Ads without editing the website code each time. Looker Studio turns the data into a dashboard anyone on your team can read.
Without conversion tracking you see traffic but not results. With it, every page, keyword and campaign can be judged by the leads it brings.

for_who.title: Signs your tracking needs work
items: You have GA4 but do not trust the numbers.
You cannot tell which pages or campaigns bring form submissions, calls or WhatsApp messages.
Your Google Ads conversions do not match what really happens.
You still look only at pageviews and sessions.
Monthly reports take hours to put together.

included.title: What the GA4 setup includes
included.intro: Five parts, tested end to end before you rely on them.

items.name: GA4 advanced configuration
items.desc: Data streams, data retention, internal traffic filters, cross-domain settings and the links to Google Ads and Search Console, set up correctly from the start.

items.name: Google Tag Manager setup
items.desc: A clean container with clear naming, so tags, triggers and variables are easy to maintain and nothing fires twice.

items.name: Custom event & conversion tracking
items.desc: Form submissions, phone and WhatsApp clicks, email clicks, bookings and other key actions tracked as events and marked as conversions.

items.name: Looker Studio dashboards
items.desc: One dashboard with leads by page, source, campaign and device, updated automatically.

items.name: Conversion funnel visualization
items.desc: A funnel report that shows where visitors drop off between landing on a page and becoming a lead.

items.title: Tracking plan
items.desc: We agree on what counts as a lead and which actions to measure.

items.title: Setup and testing
items.desc: GA4 and Google Tag Manager are configured, and every event and conversion is tested.

items.title: Dashboard
items.desc: A Looker Studio dashboard shows leads by page, source and campaign.

tools.intro: All of them are free Google tools, so there is no extra subscription to pay.

items.desc: Stores your events and conversions and reports on them.

items.desc: Sends events to GA4 and Google Ads without code changes for every update.

items.desc: Imports GA4 conversions so campaigns are measured on real leads.

compare.title: GA4 vs. Google Tag Manager
paragraphs: GA4 is where your data is stored and reported. Google Tag Manager is where tracking is configured and sent. You can run GA4 without Tag Manager, but every new event then needs a developer to edit the site.
Universal Analytics, the previous version of Google Analytics, stopped collecting data in July 2023, so GA4 is now the standard for every website.

faqs.question: Why use GA4 and Google Tag Manager together?
faqs.answer: GA4 stores and reports your data. Tag Manager is where the tracking lives, so events can be added or fixed without changing the website code each time.

faqs.question: Can you track WhatsApp and phone clicks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clicks on WhatsApp links, phone numbers and email addresses can be tracked as events and marked as conversions in GA4.

faqs.question: Does this work with Google Ads?
faqs.answer: Yes. GA4 conversions can be imported into Google Ads, so your campaigns are measured on real leads.

faqs.question: Can you fix an existing GA4 setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can review what is already in place, fix broken or duplicate events and clean up the reports.

faqs.question: How soon will I see data?
faqs.answer: Events start recording as soon as the setup is published. Useful trends appear after a few weeks of data.

faqs.question: How much does a GA4 setup cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on how many actions you want to track and how many sites or ad accounts are involved. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call.

seo-for-law-firms.title: SEO for law firms
seo-for-law-firms.lead: Get your firm found when people in your area search for a lawyer in your practice area, and turn those searches into consultations.

definition.title: What is law firm SEO?
paragraphs: Law firm SEO is the work of making a law firm appear in Google when someone searches for legal help, such as “personal injury lawyer Houston” or “divorce attorney near me”. Most of these searches name a practice area and a place, so law firm SEO is mostly local SEO applied to legal services.

Google answers these searches with ads, a map showing three firms, and then the regular results. The map depends on your Google Business Profile, your reviews and your distance from the person searching. The regular results depend on your website: one strong page per practice area and per city, a fast site, and links from trusted local and legal sources.

Legal searches are competitive because one client can be worth a lot to a firm. That is why structure matters more than volume: a clear site where each practice area has its own page does better than a large site where everything sits on one services page.

for_who.title: Signs your firm needs SEO work
items: Your firm does not appear in the map results for your main practice area in your city.
All your practice areas share one page, so none of them ranks well.
Directories list a different address or phone number for your firm.
Most new clients come from referrals or paid ads, and almost none from Google.
You serve several cities or counties with one generic page.

included.title: What law firm SEO work includes
included.intro: Six pieces of work, in the order that usually brings consultations fastest.

items.name: Practice area page structure
items.desc: One page per practice area, and per city where you have an office or serve clients. Each page explains the client's situation, what the firm does and how to get in touch. This is the structure behind the U.S. law firm case study below.

items.name: Google Business Profile for law firms
items.desc: The most precise primary category (for example “Personal injury attorney” rather than “Lawyer”), secondary categories for other practice areas, services, service area, photos and a description that follows Google's guidelines.

items.name: Legal and local citations
items.desc: Your firm's name, address and phone number made consistent across legal directories (Avvo, Justia, FindLaw, Martindale-Hubbell) and general ones (Yelp, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect).

items.name: Review routine
items.desc: A simple routine for asking satisfied clients for reviews and replying to each one, without revealing anything about the client's matter.

items.name: Technical and on-page fixes
items.desc: Titles and headings that name the practice area and the city, LegalService schema markup, fast mobile pages, and fixes for the indexing problems Search Console reports.

items.name: Lead tracking
items.desc: Calls, form submissions and consultation bookings tracked in GA4, so you know which practice area pages bring cases.

items.desc: Calls, website clicks and direction requests from the map results.

compare.title: Law firm SEO vs. Google Ads for lawyers
paragraphs: Google Ads puts your firm at the top of the page from the first day, and stops the day you stop paying. Legal keywords are among the most expensive in Google Ads, so each click can cost a firm a lot.

SEO takes months to build, but the rankings, reviews and pages keep bringing clients without a cost per click. Many firms use both: ads for immediate cases while SEO grows, then less ad spend as organic rankings take over.

faqs.question: How long does SEO take for a law firm?
faqs.answer: Fixes to your Google Business Profile and citations can show in the map results within weeks. Practice area pages and reviews build up over months. The pace depends on your city and how many firms compete for your practice area.

faqs.question: Which practice areas can you help with?
faqs.answer: Any practice area where clients search locally, such as personal injury, family law, immigration, criminal defense, estate planning or business law.

faqs.question: Do lawyer advertising rules affect SEO?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bar rules on lawyer advertising apply to your website, your profile and your review replies. Pages should not promise case outcomes, and replies to reviews should never reveal client information. Check your state bar's rules before publishing case results or testimonials.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate page for each city?
faqs.answer: If you have an office in that city or regularly serve clients there, yes. Each page needs real local details, not the same text with the city name changed.

faqs.question: How much does SEO for a law firm cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on how many practice areas and locations you have. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call, before any work starts.

faqs.question: Do you work with law firms outside the U.S.?
faqs.answer: Yes. I am based in Morocco, work remotely, and work with businesses in Morocco, the UK and the U.S., in English, French or Arabic.
